findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the grep proving command for the no-runtime-import AC to use `-E` for portable ERE alternation: `grep -En 'from rebar.llm.runner|import runner' src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py`
evidence: Plan text: `grep -n 'from rebar.llm.runner\|import runner' src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py`

On BSD grep (macOS), `\|` in a BRE pattern is a literal two-character sequence, not alternation — the command will silently match nothing and exit 1 even if a runtime import is present, producing a false negative.
Taxonomy item (3): wrong helper-script argv / flag — pattern syntax depends on grep flavor.
findings.finding: The grep proving command in the TYPE_CHECKING AC uses BRE alternation (`\|`) which is silently treated as a literal string on BSD/macOS grep, making the check a false-negative on developer machines; it should use `-E` (ERE) for portability.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — `structured_run.py has NO runtime import from runner` AC
scenarios: Developer on macOS runs the AC command and gets exit 1 (no matches found) even though a runtime import exists, incorrectly concluding the criterion is met.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the grep command with: `grep -En 'from rebar.llm.runner|import runner' src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — with `-E` the `|` is ERE alternation on both GNU and BSD grep, and the expected result is either no output (clean) or only a line inside an `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block.

evidence: Plan text: `import rebar.llm` still pulls in NO heavy module (httpx / anthropic / pydantic_ai / openai / boto3), verified empirically — heavy imports stay function-local
No shell command or Python invocation is specified to produce the evidence.
'Verified empirically' is a hedge without a proving command (E6 binary check a).
findings.finding: The heavy-import AC says 'verified empirically' but supplies no proving command; an executing agent cannot determine what command to run or what output constitutes pass/fail.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — `import rebar.llm still pulls in NO heavy module` AC
scenarios: An executor completes the split but skips the heavy-import check because no command is specified, leaving a latency regression (eager-loading a heavy SDK) undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: python -c "import sys; import rebar.llm; heavy = {'httpx','anthropic','pydantic_ai','openai','boto3'}; bad = heavy & set(sys.modules); assert not bad, f'Eager-loaded heavy modules: {bad}'"
